title: Stratified audience-based rerank model switchover with quality guards
creator: Priya Iyer
description: Goal: deploy a heterogeneous set of cross-encoder rerank variants across traffic slices (locale + audience stratum) while preserving p95 latency SLOs and preventing quality regressions. We will use stratified canaries (by locale and traffic volume), offline multilingual evals, and live automated rollback if key quality metrics drop. This ticket covers selection heuristics, runtime gating, rollout orchestration, and regression automation for the reranking endpoint.
acceptance_criteria: Canary rollout mechanism routes 1%, 5%, 20% by traffic stratum with independent metrics per stratum
Automated rollback triggers when live relevance delta (CTR-like proxy) < -2% or offline rerank NDCG drops > 0.015 vs baseline
Per-model p50/p95 token latency and GPU occupancy dashboards available in console and instrumented per-route
Fallback path implemented: when latency budget violated for a request, serve bi-encoder candidate + lightweight re-ranker fallback
Regression harness runs full multilingual benchmark (EN/ES/DE/JA/FR/KO) and reports delta in CI for every candidate model change

implementation_notes: Model selection: candidate pool contains three families - small-quantized (fast), medium-fp16 (balanced), heavy-fp16 (highest quality). Each family has per-locale calibration coeffs from offline evals.
Gating: runtime uses a composite key (locale, customer_tier, request_hash) to deterministically pick model variant. Percentages configurable per-route in rollout manifest.
Latency guard: request is passed through a cheap predictor estimating rerank latency given sequence length and batch backlog. If predicted latency > threshold, switch to fallback pipeline.
Fallback pipeline: bi-encoder candidate generation + 256-token lightweight cross-encoder rescoring (or heuristic scorer if severe overload), ensures graceful degradation.
Regression checks: CI runs multilingual NDCG/Recall + synthetic-noise perturbation suite. Live regression watch compares canary cohort to baseline for 24h before each step increase.
KV cache warmstart: for locale-heavy traffic, pre-warm token KV slices for frequent prefixes to reduce p95. Instrumentation added to measure warmstart hit-rate.
Costs: heavy variants ~2.8x token-cost of medium; gating policy tries to limit heavy usage to top 15% of traffic where quality uplift justifies cost.

Operational playbook: manual pause/rollback endpoints in Console + automated rollback policy tied to alerts. Runbook: ENG oncall paged -> narrow the cohort -> rollback model -> create postmortem if outage > 30 mins.
Canary metric set: per-cohort NDCG, approximation-CTR, p50/p95 latency, GPU mem pressure, batch size distribution, KV warmstart hit-rate. Thresholds in rollout manifest.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Heavier cross-encoders improve quality but increase p95 latency and cost. Trade-off: keep heavy models constrained to high-value strata and rely on medium model elsewhere.
Locale-specific long-tail sequences (e.g., Japanese customer support transcripts) cause latency spikes — mitigated by sequence-length gating and KV warmstarts but not fully eliminable.
Automated rollback relies on live metric signal; noisy signals can cause flapping. We add minimum observation windows and hysteresis before rollback.
Quantized variants reduce cost but may introduce calibration drift. Offline calibration steps and periodic calibration jobs are necessary post-deploy.
